I'm 70 years old, been working this land 50 years. My 5 mu isn't much but it feeds the family and gives some grain to sell. Two of my grown children work in town now, so at busy times I hire a neighbor with a tractor. Let me think about this year.

**Wheat (winter):** Last year I got about 500 jin per mu (250 kg), which was alright. I'll plant Jimai improved variety again — the seed dealer in town sells it, my neighbors use it too, no reason to change. For fertilizer at sowing I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer (50 jin, that's 25 kg) per mu as base, and then at green-up in spring I top-dress with urea, maybe 30 jin (15 kg) per mu. That works out to around 18 kg N, 9 kg P, 7 kg K per mu. I know some say to use less but wheat eats a lot and if the spike is small I lose money — better to put a little extra than come up short. Well water: I'll irrigate at sowing if dry, then over-winter water, green-up, and filling — about 3-4 times. Pesticide twice, once for aphids and powdery mildew in spring, once for the stink bug later. Rotary till before sowing, same as always.

**Maize (summer):** After wheat harvest in June I go straight into maize, no plough, just no-till seeding right into the stubble — saves time and money on tractor work, and the machine in our village does this now. Zhengdan hybrid seed, that's what works here. I apply one bag of compound at sowing (50 jin) and top-dress urea at big-trumpet stage, maybe 40 jin (20 kg) per mu — maize is hungry. About 20 kg N, 6 kg P, 5 kg K. Irrigation once or twice from the well depending on rain in July-August. Pesticide twice for corn borer and armyworm. Last year maize gave me around 600 jin (300 kg per mu), I hope for similar.

I don't want to change much — what I did last year worked, grain prices are uncertain, and every bag of fertilizer is 150 yuan.
